title: Game 3: Janowski–Capablanca
subtitle: A missed defensive plan leads to a lost pawn ending

narration.say: Janowski has White against Capablanca at Havana in 1913. Black chooses an irregular development scheme.
White castles and develops the rook while Black manoeuvres.
White challenges the bishop and exchanges in the centre.
Black exchanges on e4 instead of castling. Capablanca calls this a serious mistake.
White activates the queen and advances b4. Further exchanges leave Black’s king defending the centre.

steps.title: A plan that exchanges can neutralise

narration.say: White doubles rooks on the d-file. Black advances g5, but does not follow the defensive plan consistently.
The last pair of rooks is exchanged. Black recaptures with the knight.
White can now challenge the kingside pawns.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Challenge Black’s pawn on g5.

feedback.*: Advance the h-pawn from h3 to h4.

exercise.hint: Advance the h-pawn from h3 to h4.

steps.title: Win a pawn with active queen play

narration.say: White recaptures with check and keeps the black king exposed.
Black brings the queen to d6. White advances c5, and Black centralises the queen.
White can attack the queen with the e-pawn.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Attack the queen on d5 with a pawn advance.

narration.say: White answers the check and offers a queen exchange.
Black develops the knight. White exchanges central pawns and recaptures with the knight.
White advances the kingside majority while Black seeks queenside counterplay.
The king supports the pawns. White exchanges the remaining knights while Black takes queenside pawns.

steps.title: The pawn advance cannot be stopped

narration.say: White advances f5 and f6. Black gives a knight check, but the king steps to h6.
Black resigns. The two advanced passed pawns decide the ending.

steps.title: Carry out the plan you chose

narration.say: Capablanca repeatedly identifies g6 as an important defensive idea that he failed to carry out.
White converted the resulting pawn weakness through queen activity, favourable exchanges and supported passed pawns.
The opening, middle-game and ending are connected: a choice in one phase can determine the next.
